prompt:
Create an ENTIRELY NEW photorealistic portrait gardening photograph from these original real camera references. Start the scene, human anatomy, pose, lighting and watering can from scratch. This is a new photograph for a British vegetable gardening book's "Growing Techniques" opener, not a patch of a previous generated picture. No previous generated scene is supplied.

COMPOSITION: Portrait 185:240. A low camera looks across an abundant but natural bed of mixed green and burgundy salad leaves: lettuces, rocket and mustard, growing irregularly, with occasional small gaps showing dark soil. Leaves fill the lower two-thirds and both sides, with interest distributed across the frame and no isolated hero plant. Farther back on a narrow path at the upper right, the real man shown in the references waters the far end of the bed. Keep him visibly behind the plants, a secondary background actor. His visible figure from head to knee occupies about 35–40% of the total image height. Show his head comfortably inside the upper-right frame with a little green background above. Keep the upper-left as quiet foliage texture, with a few ordinary weathered cane and green mesh supports in the middle distance. No buildings or sky. Soft overcast natural early-summer daylight, genuine ordinary Cornish garden character, documentary photography. The man must remain recognisable, naturally detailed rather than blurred to conceal anatomy.

REFERENCE ROLES:
1: REAL watering photograph. This is the primary authority for anatomically normal ARM LENGTHS, real joints, compact working posture, the weight of the can, TWO-HANDED GRIP, and a physically real moulded watering-can design. Rebuild that human action faithfully, seen in a similar left-facing three-quarter side view, holding the can close in front of his waist/upper thighs. The can in this photo is blue; use its real construction but make it a muted garden GREEN. Do not bring over the plaid shirt, woodpile, shed, or bare bed.
2: REAL summer wardrobe and physique. Same man, his normal mature build, olive short-sleeve T-shirt, olive shorts, bareheaded, short greying hair with a receding forehead. Use his actual shoulder/torso/arm proportions. No hat, microphone, clothing text or presentation gesture.
3: REAL bareheaded left profile: identity, actual nose bridge and rounded tip, lips, chin, beard, ear and hairline.
4: Mandatory lowered-profile sheet: use the first THREE real camera stills, especially the upper-left real lowered left-profile. The lower-right illustration is NOT an anatomical reference and must be ignored.
5: REAL allotment: ordinary small-scale garden character, soil, modest canes and supports, natural planting. Use a tighter foliage-filled viewpoint; exclude sheds and houses.

ANATOMY AND ACTION, VITAL: Draw the whole person as one coherent body. Both upper arms have normal, comparable lengths; elbows sit naturally near the waist. Both forearms have normal lengths and bend towards the can in a comfortable compact pose. Both hands hold REAL load-bearing handle parts at the top/rear of the can, as in the original watering photograph. Keep the can close to his body and move the can to meet the hands naturally. No long reaching arm, elongated forearm, doubled elbow, stretched wrist, hand coming from an unseen extra arm, or hand appearing underneath the can on an abnormally long limb. The person stands balanced on the far path, leaning only slightly forwards, calmly looking down-left at where he is watering. The two hands and genuine handles must be clearly connected and physically plausible at normal scale.

WATERING CAN: faithfully use the simple real moulded-plastic construction from camera reference 1, recoloured muted green. A modest real container, one genuine carrying/tilting handle assembly attached to its body, filling opening and one tapered spout that emerges from the low front of the body and ends in a black rose. Hands must grip real handle surfaces attached to the body. No invented bar linking the hand to the spout, no supplementary pole, no extraneous third handle, no warped or floating components. Tilt the can so a gentle spray falls from the black rose down towards the soil among plants at the far edge of the bed.

LIKELINESS: match the REAL man in references 2–4 accurately, including the real rounded nose-tip/profile. With his head looking down, his lower lip is farther forward than his chin; the chin recedes beneath the mouth and the short grey beard slopes backwards towards the throat. Do not invent a jutting square chin, a rounded forward beard extension, a hooked pointy nose, a heroic jaw or sunken eyes. Natural older adult appearance, without beautification or caricature.

Natural leafy textures, varied leaf sizes, believable hands and gardening equipment. No typography, no oval, no borders, no labels, no contact sheet, no inset. ONE new full-page photograph.
